live_issue.title: [v0.92.1][Runtime] Support TLS 1.2 on public Axum HTTPS/WSS for Unity
live_issue.body:
## Problem

Runtime v3's public Axum HTTPS/WSS listener is hard-coded to TLS 1.3 only. Unity 6000.5.1f1's UnityTLS client negotiates TLS 1.2 with otherwise compatible public endpoints and cannot complete the Runtime handshake. This blocks issue #84 even with a valid CA-issued certificate and complete Let’s Encrypt chain.

The restriction is currently explicit in `adl-runtime-kernel/src/tls.rs` through `with_protocol_versions(&[&rustls::version::TLS13])`.

## Diagnostic evidence

The #84 native Unity Play Mode lane established the following controls:

- Unity accepted Let’s Encrypt's official X2-terminating Gen-Y test endpoint.
- Unity rejected direct Root YE trust, as expected.
- A separately issued short-lived ECDSA Wuji leaf with the same YE/X2 certificate shape still failed against the ADL Runtime with UnityTLS error code 7.
- The exact Wuji short-lived leaf and chain succeeded when served by OpenSSL on the same host and port. Unity negotiated TLS 1.2 and advanced past certificate validation to the expected application-layer timeout.
- Therefore the certificate, hostname, ECDSA key, and X2 chain are not the blocker; the Runtime's TLS 1.3-only public listener is the discriminating boundary.

Retained local evidence in the #84 worktree includes:

- `.adl/evidence/84/unity-runtime-v3/20260812T063900Z-live.log` — official X2 endpoint accepted at TLS layer.
- `.adl/evidence/84/unity-runtime-v3/20260812T064625Z-live.log` — short-lived Wuji certificate rejected against Runtime.
- `.adl/evidence/84/unity-runtime-v3/20260812T064949Z-live.log` — identical Wuji certificate presentation accepted through OpenSSL; application layer intentionally non-Runtime.

## Required outcome

Support TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 on Runtime v3's public Axum HTTPS/WSS listener using the shared reviewed Rustls provider and secure ECDHE cipher suites, while preserving TLS 1.3-only behavior for Quinn Guardian transport where that is a protocol invariant.

## Acceptance criteria

- Public Axum HTTPS/WSS server configuration enables both Rustls TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.
- TLS 1.2 support is limited to reviewed forward-secret AEAD suites compatible with the configured ECDSA and RSA certificate policies; no legacy TLS versions or weak suites are enabled.
- Quinn Guardian mTLS remains TLS 1.3-only unless a separate reviewed requirement changes it.
- Focused tests prove the public listener accepts TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 and rejects TLS 1.1 and earlier.
- Focused tests cover CA-issued ECDSA identity loading and complete-chain presentation without leaf-as-root trust.
- The real Unity 6000.5.1f1 Play Mode product adapter completes HTTPS and WSS authentication against the Runtime without a proxy, trust-store mutation, custom always-accept certificate handler, or verification bypass.
- Existing browser/curl clients continue to negotiate TLS 1.3 when supported.
- Runtime startup remains fail-closed for invalid identity, incomplete chain, wrong SAN, expiry, unsuitable EKU, and unknown issuer.
- Observability records negotiated TLS version without logging credentials or certificate private material.

## Non-goals

- Disabling certificate validation or adding a Unity-specific trust bypass.
- Installing or mutating host keychain trust.
- Adding a TLS-termination proxy as the product solution.
- Weakening Quinn Guardian mutual authentication.
- Reissuing certificates as a substitute for protocol compatibility.
- Implementing this change inside issue #84.

## Issue graph

- Follow-up to closed TLS standardization issue #92.
- Blocks the real native Unity acceptance lane and publication of #84.
- #84 owns only the Unity consumer and must treat this Runtime change as an upstream dependency.

Canonical successor for [danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5845](https://github.com/danielbaustin/agent-design-language/issues/5845).

## Migration semantics

## Archived source issue body

## Summary

Execute **WP-24A** for v0.92 within this issue's approved design and ownership boundary.

Create and validate ten review-ready production packages using retained Podcast Studio v2 proof and the approved route/storage decision. Complete episode checkpoints may land incrementally, but a checkpoint must include the full package contract for every episode it labels complete. Do not close WP-24A until all ten packages and the integration proof are complete.

## Required Outcome

All first ten episodes are complete review-ready production packages, not topic or schema placeholders.

## Episode Package Contract

Each complete episode includes canonical episode metadata, source packet, script, transcript, show notes, final MP3 and archive audio with manifests, QA report, guest metadata, artwork and ID3 metadata, RSS enclosure record, redaction report, and editorial/audio review.

Shared audio routes are allowed when the episode metadata, audio manifest, and enclosure record bind the exact paths, byte counts, and SHA-256 digests.

An incremental checkpoint:

- includes the complete package for each episode it claims;
- passes the applicable positive and negative validators;
- uses `Part of danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5845`, not a closing keyword;
- leaves this parent issue open.

## Deliverables

- Ten complete episode directories
- Ten final MP3 and archive-audio artifacts with manifests
- Validated feed and enclosure records
- Audio, redaction, guest, metadata, playback, and listen-check QA
- Exact-head editorial/audio review

## Dependencies

- #5819 canonical naming/link truth
- #3223 and #3256 retained Podcast Studio v2 proof
- Agent Logic route/storage decision

## Validation And Proof

- Prove complete package contents, audio manifests, embedded ID3 metadata, and feed/enclosure parity.
- Reject missing audio or package artifacts, digest and metadata mismatch, local feed paths, guest-acceptance overclaims, unsafe text, and publication overclaims.
- Retain source-SHA-bound platform playback evidence before terminal WP-24A completion.
- Keep deployment, mailbox verification, branded-host configuration, directory submission, and publication under the separate launch authority.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC-1: All ten episodes contain every required script, audio, transcript, note, metadata, artwork, enclosure, redaction, QA, and review artifact.
- AC-2: Audio digests, duration, sample rate, channels, loudness, peak, ID3/artwork, listen check, and archive records are internally consistent.
- AC-3: Feed/enclosure records match episode specs and reject local paths, drafts, unstable GUIDs, missing bytes, and MIME/duration mismatches.
- AC-4: Guest consent, source rights, credentials, synthetic-voice provenance, and redaction remain truthful and privacy-safe.
- AC-5: Required source-SHA-bound platform playback receipts pass digest-recomputing validation before terminal completion, with no deployment or publication claim.

## Non-Goals

- Deployment or podcast-directory submission
- Mailbox verification
- Branded-host configuration
- Treating historical smoke artifacts as final
- Claiming guest acceptance, live unscripted dialogue, weekly cadence, or a public route without proof
- Article ownership

## Rollback

Restore the previous feed and launch-readiness records, remove only episode packages and playback producers introduced by this issue, and retain rejected audio, redaction, consent, metadata, and playback reports under issue evidence. Rollback must not delete upstream Podcast Studio proof, mutate guest consent records, deploy feed changes, or claim publication.

live_issue.body:
Canonical successor for [danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5907](https://github.com/danielbaustin/agent-design-language/issues/5907).

## Migration semantics

- `replaces`: danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5907 as active current-repository issue authority.
- The archived source body is preserved below without claiming implementation, review, publication, merge, or terminal progress.
- Continue all future planning and lifecycle work only on this current-repository successor.

## Archived source issue body

## Purpose

Preserve and complete the AWS GPU Shepherd proof work formerly carried in PR
`agent-logic/agent-design-language#72` without widening the local-only contract
of #5795.

This is a separate optional remote-proof lane. It does not replace or gate the
required local Chrome -> Observatory -> governed Runtime -> Shepherd acceptance
path in #5795.

## Recoverable Source

The initial implementation is retained in commit
`7a26886c47962e71c128489f5176a045ae8e9a64` on branch
`codex/5795-local-gemma-mlx-shepherd`, primarily:

- `adl/tools/run_wp5795_aws_gpu_proof.sh`
- `.csdlc/evidence/5795/foundation/aws-gpu-preflight.json`
- `.csdlc/evidence/5795/foundation/aws-deadline-reaper.json`
- `.csdlc/evidence/5795/foundation/aws-lock-collision.json`
- related AWS proof receipts in `.csdlc/evidence/5795/`

Recover this work from Git history; do not keep it inside the final #5795 diff.

## Independent Sequence

1. WP-14 #5832 freezes the protocol contract.
2. #5795 completes the governed local Shepherd and browser round trip.
3. This issue consumes the terminal local adapter contract and runs the optional
   AWS GPU portability proof.

Preparation that touches only this issue's future owned paths may proceed
independently. Paid AWS execution and final proof must use the terminal #5795
adapter revision. This issue has its own worktree, branch, PR, focused proof,
review, and closeout. It must not share mutable worktree state with either
#5832 or #5795.

## Required Outcome

Provide a bounded, repeatable AWS GPU proof runner for the Shepherd model
adapter using the approved Agent Logic business AWS account and permanent
operator-provisioned IAM profile.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The AWS runner is a single reusable project command with explicit launch,
  exact-revision, proof, and cleanup predicates.
- It uses the approved Agent Logic AWS profile and verifies the resolved
  business account before mutation.
- It requires an explicitly named no-ingress security group and verifies the
  effective ingress contract before launch.
- It verifies the exact expected instance profile, role, and required policy
  contract rather than accepting any attached role.
- It proves model-backed Shepherd execution at the requested repository
  revision and retains machine-readable evidence.
- It terminates the instance and associated temporary resources on success,
  failure, interruption, and deadline expiry.
- It records cost-relevant runtime and instance details without exposing
  credentials or secrets.
- Focused negative proofs cover lock collision, invalid IAM/security-group
  configuration, stale revision, and cleanup failure.
- Documentation clearly states this is an optional remote proof and is not part
  of #5795's local-only acceptance contract.

## Non-Goals

- Changing #5795's local-only acceptance criteria.
- Making AWS a required runtime dependency or production inference fallback.
- Creating IAM profiles, roles, or security groups inside the runner.
- Using the personal/default AWS account.
